headline: Shift Large User Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Approved by Governor-Chapter 1123 (effective 7/1/2026) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, customer advocates, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Senator Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (initially, for the bill as passed by GA).
opponents: Data centers, large manufacturers (who would face increased costs), potentially Governor Spanberger's office (due to amendments perceived as weakening the bill).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money. Critics argue the governor's amendments, which broaden the SCC's discretion rather than prescribing specific cost-shifting mechanisms, may weaken the bill's original intent to protect ratepayers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill directs water utilities to report aggregate estimates of water consumption by data centers, providing transparency on their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, community advocates, Senator Srinivasan (sponsor).
opponents: Not explicitly mentioned as having strong opposition, as it's a reporting bill. Data center industry might prefer less scrutiny, but no direct opposition found.
news_headline: Data Center Bills Dominated This Year's General Assembly. Here's What Passed.
news_summary: SB 553, which directs water utilities to report aggregate estimates of water consumption by data centers, cleared both chambers and is under consideration by the Governor. This measure aims to provide transparency on data center water usage, allowing for comparisons with other industrial and commercial sectors.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires high-energy-use data centers to provide localities with noise impact assessments and allows localities to require site assessments for impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Community groups, environmental advocates, Delegate Josh Thomas (sponsor), Senator Danica Roem (for companion SB 94).
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased regulatory burden and potential siting restrictions).
news_headline: New governor could see new versions of old bills seeking to regulate the data center industry
news_summary: HB 153, sponsored by Delegate Thomas, passed the House and requires high-energy-use data center developers to conduct site assessments for noise impact on residences and schools within 500 feet. It also allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water resources, agriculture, and historic sites.
